claims.sentence:
All morning people have been asking me about a blog post by Matt Shumer that
has gone viral.
claims.reason: Claims the post went viral, a verifiable popularity/attention claim.

claims.sentence:
It is a masterpiece of hype, written in the style of old
direct marketing campaigns, with bold-faced call outs like “I know this is
real because it happened to me first” and “I am no longer needed for the
actual technical work of my job”.
claims.reason: Attributes specific direct quotes to Shumer's blog post that can be verified against the original.

claims.sentence:
He
> gives no actual data to support this claim that the latest coding systems
> can write whole complex apps without making errors.
claims.reason: Testable claim about absence of supporting data in Shumer's post.

claims.sentence:
Similarly, when he
> describes how AIs are doing longer and longer tasks on METR’s famous
> task-time benchmark, he neglects to say the criterion on that benchmark is
> 50% correct, not 100%, and that the benchmark is only about coding and not
> tasks in general.
claims.reason: Specific factual claim about METR benchmark methodology that can be verified against METR's published criteria.

claims.sentence:
No AI system can reliably do every five-hour long task
> humans can do without error, or even close.
claims.reason: A measurable, testable claim about current AI system capabilities.

claims.sentence:
Shumer ignored a different METR study where coders sometimes imagined
   productivity gains while actually losing productivity.
claims.reason: References a specific study with a testable finding that can be checked for existence and content.

claims.sentence: Other users do not report “it’s usually perfect.”
claims.reason: A factual claim about user reports/reviews that can be checked against actual user testimonials.
